newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 9.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
'PAY WOMEN TO HELP CHILDLESS HAVE BABIES'

Professor Ian Craft, director of the London Gynaecology and Fertility Centre has stirred up the surrogacy debate by saying that women who donate eggs for childless couples should be paid up to 450 stg a time. However, the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority intends to phase out all payments for egg donation.
WONTNERS READY TO SELL STAKE IN SAVOY

The Wontners and its charitable trusts which controls the Savoy Group looks set to be persuaded by Granada to relinquish its stake in the company. Younger members of the family are keen to convert their holding into cash which would mean that The Savoy Group could then be sold complete.

Leading accountancy firm KPMG has suggested that huge savings could be made by Lloyd's if it scraps the traditional system whereby syndicates raise new capital each year to support underwriting. Lloyd's Corporate Capital Association commissioned a study outlining the reforms.
JAPANESE RATE RISE HINT RATTLES DOLLAR
For the first time in over a month the greenback fell below 123 yen, in anticipation of higher Japanese interest rates.
SAM FINDS FAVOUR AND DELIGHTS BoS
The Bank of Scotland has had great success with its

Shared Appreciation Mortgages which it launched in November. 2000 borrowers, the maximum take up target has been reached, for the loans which offer a fixed for life 0 percent or 5.75 percent interest rate mortgage in return for a share of any capital appreciation in the value of the house on which the loan was taken out.
